headline: Profit surges as truck build rates and freight rates improve
summary_short: PACCAR grew Q2 FY2026 net income 24% q/q and 4% y/y to $752.0 million ($1.43 diluted EPS), as revenue rose 11% q/q to $7.55 billion on higher truck build rates and record PACCAR Parts revenue of $1.75 billion.
summary_long: Net income rose 24% q/q and 4% y/y to $752.0M ($1.43 diluted EPS) as build rates increased on strong orders and improved freight rates. Revenue grew 11% q/q and 0.5% y/y to $7.55B; gross profit grew 17% q/q to $1.32B and operating income grew 30% q/q to $879.2M, outpacing revenue as R&D and SG&A fell slightly q/q. PACCAR Parts posted record revenue of $1.75B with pre-tax income of $417.0M, and Financial Services pre-tax income rose to $124.1M on steady finance margins and an improving used-truck market. Cash fell to $8.67B from $9.25B at year-end after $1.09B of first-half dividends and debt paydown. PACCAR guided FY2026 capex to $700-750M and R&D to $450-480M.

drivers.explanation: CEO Feight attributed the 24% q/q increase to higher build rates, driven by strong orders as customers benefited from improved freight rates.
Revenue growth reflects the same build-rate increase, as customers responded to constrained freight capacity and higher freight rates by ordering more trucks.
Gross profit grew faster than revenue (17% vs 11% q/q) as cost of sales rose only about 11% q/q, expanding gross margin slightly.
Operating income outgrew gross profit because combined R&D and SG&A fell about $6M q/q even as gross profit rose $195M.
EPS growth tracked net income growth closely since diluted share count was essentially flat q/q at about 527.6 million shares.
PACCAR Parts posted record quarterly revenue on an improving North American freight market; PACCAR Financial Services grew on steady finance margins and a stronger used-truck market.
